one_line: Local-first registry and runtime turns reviewed action packs into WebMCP tools inside signed-in sites.
what_it_does: Lets users adopt typed, origin-bound, safety-wrapped WebMCP action packs for sites lacking APIs, with human authorization for writes.
leverage_rationale: The claimed product addresses the central gap between authenticated browser state and reliable agent actions; reviewed declarative packs, bounded output, drift failure, and human authorization are materially beyond blind UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Pitch frames an existing signed-in tab as the API.
Description claims exact-origin reviewed fingerprints, declarative JSON manifests, bounded untrusted output, and human authority on consequences.
execution_rationale: The concept and safety architecture are unusually coherent, but the packet provides no video and the visual evidence could not be inspected, so end-to-end execution is only claimed.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are listed.
Description presents a concrete local-first registry/runtime workflow.
impact_rationale: Operations teams working in API-less authenticated consoles have a specific, credible automation problem, and the proposed adoption model could generalize across many sites.
impact_evidence: Description identifies Grafana, Cal.com, payer portals, vendor consoles, and admin dashboards as target contexts.
Claims measurement of 3 open-source products and 429 candidate tool locations.
creativity_rationale: Reframing the user's existing login/session as an adoptable API and distributing reviewed action packs is a memorable, ambitious inversion of vendor-led API adoption.
creativity_evidence: Core reframe is explicitly described as one user, one tab, one reviewed pack at a time.
Safety properties are integrated into the interaction model rather than presented as a generic agent wrapper.
usability_note: Potentially clear for pack installation and authorization, but unverified visually.
red_flags: No submitted video; visual claims could not be checked.
About text is truncated in the packet.
standouts: WebMCP is central rather than cosmetic.
advance_reason: High leverage and originality with a credible broad operations use case; execution needs observation.

one_line: Shared USDA hardiness-zone lookup and garden-planning map for people and agents.
what_it_does: Provides zone lookup, plant suitability, frost windows, planting calendars, and a garden plan through UI, WebMCP tools, and JSON APIs.
leverage_rationale: Structured authoritative zone data and shared state improve agent reliability over PDFs and guessed location facts, though a general agent could accomplish much of the lookup with friction.
leverage_evidence: Claims coverage of 40,502 ZIP codes and 54 plants.
Lists 18 WebMCP tools and writes that change what the human sees, including confirmation and geolocation permission flows.
execution_rationale: The described scope is substantial and internally coherent, but no video is submitted and visual execution cannot be verified.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are listed.
Description names UI, WebMCP, backend API, OpenAPI, and llms.txt surfaces.
impact_rationale: Gardeners have a concrete recurring need for accurate local growing guidance; surfacing the authoritative USDA map with actionable planting planning is a credible fit.
impact_evidence: Specific gardener question and USDA source problem are articulated.
Plant ratings and planting calendar connect lookup to action.
creativity_rationale: It is a fresh agent-native packaging of an awkward authoritative reference, with shared map state and garden planning extending beyond a simple lookup.
creativity_evidence: Combines authoritative map data, agent tools, and human-visible garden-plan mutations.
Positions itself as a primitive for future weather and sun-position planning.
usability_note: Clear ZIP/location-to-plan journey is claimed; visual verification unavailable.
red_flags: No submitted video; visual claims could not be checked.
standouts: Human and agent share map/planning state.
advance_reason: Strong audience fit and meaningful WebMCP use; advance for breadth and verify execution later.

one_line: Local browser document workspace where an agent finds pages, merges files, and downloads a named packet.
what_it_does: Reads local PDFs, identifies relevant pages, extracts and merges them in order, and downloads a privacy-preserving application packet.
leverage_rationale: Typed document operations let an agent reason over and manipulate local files deterministically; blind UI automation cannot comparably reliably find pages, preserve order, and name outputs.
leverage_evidence: Description gives an end-to-end visa-packet example with page discovery and merge ordering.
Claims all operations execute client-side and files never leave the tab.
execution_rationale: The workflow is concrete and complete in description, but absent video and unavailable frame inspection limit claimed-execution confidence.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo listed.
Specific input, discovery, merge, naming, and download sequence is described.
impact_rationale: Applicants for visas, rentals, and insurance face a real tedious and privacy-sensitive document-preparation problem; this directly reduces both manual effort and cloud-upload exposure.
impact_evidence: Target audiences and recurring PDF workflow are explicit.
Privacy benefit is architectural rather than a policy promise.
creativity_rationale: The combination of local-only documents and agentic semantic page selection is a strong, memorable application of WebMCP to a mundane high-friction workflow.
creativity_evidence: Agent reads a bank statement and selects salary pages without typed page numbers.
Local execution changes the privacy tradeoff.
usability_note: Natural-language goal plus deterministic document tools is promising; not visually verified.
red_flags: No video inspection available; packet has no transcript.
advance_reason: Excellent concrete impact and strong WebMCP delta; execution should be observed in the next stage.

one_line: Small home-goods shop with a shared human-agent cart and explicit purchase approval.
what_it_does: Lets an agent recommend gifts and stage cart changes while the human sees the same state, approves, reviews, and confirms purchases.
leverage_rationale: Shared live cart state and explicit approval make agent shopping more reliable and legible than a parallel agent page or guessed clicks, though the underlying shopping task remains UI-replicable.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and description emphasize same tab, same cart, and no purchase without approval.
Named tools include account, saved customer, shop state, and gift recommendation.
execution_rationale: The packet contains packaging/gallery text describing the flow but no video frames, so the central purchase workflow is only partially evidenced.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are listed.
Description specifies recommendation, tradeoff card, approval, review, and confirmation stages.
impact_rationale: Gift shoppers have a recognizable desire for help with discovery and tradeoffs while retaining control over purchases; the small-shop setting gives the concept a credible focused audience.
impact_evidence: Concrete under-£40 cooking gift scenario.
Human approval boundary directly addresses unintended purchases.
creativity_rationale: The shared-cart and proposal-before-mutation interaction is a thoughtful inversion of opaque AI shopping demos, though the shop category itself is familiar.
creativity_evidence: recommend_gift produces a tradeoff card and leaves cart empty until approval.
Human and agent operate on one visible cart.
usability_note: Approval-oriented flow sounds understandable; no visual proof available.
red_flags: Packet evidence is largely text/gallery packaging.
standouts: Shared state is central to the product pitch.
advance_reason: Meaningful shared-cart pattern and credible niche value, with limited execution evidence.

one_line: Agent-native grocery planner that optimizes meals and baskets under budget and allergy constraints.
what_it_does: Plans meals, builds and optimizes a seeded grocery basket, finds substitutions, validates allergies, and pauses for human approval.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools can encode budget, allergy, substitution, and approval constraints more reliably than an agent clicking a grocery site, but the seeded demo remains broadly reproducible with conventional software APIs.
leverage_evidence: Description says constraints are encoded directly in nine WebMCP tools.
Demo scenario detects peanut product, substitutes safely, optimizes under budget, and requests approval.
execution_rationale: The described demo is coherent, but there are no gallery images or video frames and no public repository, so claimed completeness is weakly evidenced.
execution_evidence: Live demo is listed.
Specific seeded products, household, budget, diet, allergy, and outcome are provided.
impact_rationale: Budgeting meals around allergies and pantry inventory is a real recurring household problem, and the safety focus gives the tool credible value.
impact_evidence: Explicit target constraints include budget, diet, allergies, pantry items, and store preference.
No payment is processed and final basket requires approval.
creativity_rationale: A competent synthesis of agentic grocery planning with safety and optimization; the interaction has a useful angle but is less novel than the strongest packets.
creativity_evidence: Combines meal planning, price comparison, substitutions, allergy validation, and approval.
Uses WebMCP as typed constraint-bearing workflow tools.
usability_note: Constraint-first flow is plausible but unverified and likely depends on seeded demo data.
red_flags: No public repository, gallery images, or video frames.
standouts: Allergy safety is treated as a first-class constraint.
advance_reason: Credible use case but insufficient evidence and only moderate novelty for this review stage.

one_line: Agent-enabled explorable Hoenn-inspired world with walking, conversations, and landscape exploration.
what_it_does: Reimplements an Emerald-like world in JavaScript, allowing zoomed-out free exploration and agent interaction.
leverage_rationale: Agents can add conversational or navigation convenience to a playable world, but ordinary UI/game automation can achieve comparable outcomes; WebMCP is not shown as structurally necessary.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes an interactive map where users walk, talk, and explore with an agent.
Description frames the main innovation as creative-mode exploration rather than structured shared state.
execution_rationale: The claimed adaptation has a defined scope and acknowledges responsiveness/tick challenges, but no video frames or repository evidence are provided.
execution_evidence: Live demo and five gallery images are listed.
Description states a parity-oriented JS reimplementation and discusses map responsiveness.
impact_rationale: There is a real audience among fans and ROM-hack communities seeking exploratory game experiences, though the value is primarily entertainment and homage.
impact_evidence: Explicit Pokemon Emerald fan and ROM-hacking audience.
Creative-mode exploration is a clear stated desire.
creativity_rationale: A faithful game adaptation combined with zoomed-out creative-mode exploration and agent interaction is a fresh synthesis, even if based on an existing property.
creativity_evidence: Positions itself between emulation and free-roam creative exploration.
Agent can participate in walking, conversations, and exploration.
usability_note: Game-like exploration is likely approachable; agent interaction and completeness unverified.
red_flags: No public repository and no video frames.
Uses a faithful adaptation of an existing game/property; origin and scope need scrutiny.
standouts: Clear emotional connection to a defined fan community.
advance_reason: Creative game concept, but WebMCP delta and execution evidence are too weak.

one_line: Shared decision room where one browser AI supplies six named perspectives and a human controls approval.
what_it_does: Maintains a revisioned brief, gathers role-based contributions, prepares recommendations, and records human decisions with evidence.
leverage_rationale: Shared revisioned state, named role requests, evidence-linked contributions, stale-recommendation handling, and exact decision records are difficult to reproduce reliably through UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Seven WebMCP tools share persistence/API logic with UI actions.
Description specifies expectedRevision optimistic concurrency and operationId safe retries.
Budget revision invalidates prior recommendation without rewriting history.
execution_rationale: The workflow and state model are unusually well specified, and a transcript supports the core progression, though screenshots/video frames remain unavailable for independent visual verification.
execution_evidence: Transcript describes changing budget, diagnosis of stale recommendation, new recommendation, and human review.
Description identifies concrete tools and persistence behavior.
impact_rationale: Founders and decision teams have a real need to compare perspectives under changing constraints while preserving rationale and authority.
impact_evidence: Specific founder decision-room audience and consequential decisions are stated.
Visible alternatives, reservations, evidence, and approval states address the stated problem.
creativity_rationale: The stateful boardroom metaphor, six explicit perspectives, revision-aware recommendations, and human-controlled decision record form a fresh interaction model.
creativity_evidence: One browser AI adopts six named specialist roles without pretending to be six model workers.
Decision history remains intact as constraints change.
usability_note: Visible review and explicit approval boundaries suggest a clear workflow; visual inspection unavailable.
red_flags: No public repository and only one gallery image.
Transcript is evidence supplied by submission, not independent observation.
standouts: Human decision authority is explicit and preserved.
advance_reason: High WebMCP leverage with credible decision-workflow impact and strong conceptual execution.

one_line: Agent-native vehicle configurator, synchronized garage twin, owner guide, and 3D creation engine.
what_it_does: Lets agents and humans configure a fictional vehicle, inspect pricing and components, direct a shared 3D model, and explore measurement-driven construction.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools across five contexts, shared 3D state, measurable component inspection, revision-gated undoable mutations, and interruption handling make agent collaboration substantially more reliable than pointer automation.
leverage_evidence: Description claims 49 registrations across landing, configurator, garage, guide, and creation contexts.
Mutations are revision-gated and undoable; results state source or measurement basis.
Agent can reveal and measure 42 named components.
execution_rationale: The breadth and named technical/testing stack indicate intentional scope, but no video transcript and unavailable frame inspection reduce certainty about end-to-end polish.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are listed.
Description names React/Three.js UI, Vitest, Playwright, and five integrated contexts.
impact_rationale: Car buyers and enthusiasts can benefit from understandable configuration, ownership outcomes, and inspectable vehicle information, though the fictional vehicle narrows immediate practical reach.
impact_evidence: Configurator, garage digital twin, owner guide, pricing, and ownership outcomes are explicitly targeted.
Fictional reconstruction is honestly disclosed.
creativity_rationale: The ambitious combination of a 3D configurator, synchronized digital twin, visual guide, and code-native creation engine is unusually deep and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Five page contexts and 49 tools pursue one coherent agent-native vehicle concept.
Measurement-driven model-building workflow is exposed as part of the product.
usability_note: Rich contexts may be powerful but risk complexity; no visual verification.
red_flags: No gallery images and no transcript; visual product claims could not be checked.
Fictional car limits direct real-world purchasing applicability.
advance_reason: Ambitious, creative, and technically coherent WebMCP integration warrants advancement despite incomplete visual evidence.

one_line: Socratic exam coach whose site architecture controls knowledge, tool access, mastery gates, and exam mode.
what_it_does: Provides constrained coaching, deterministic misconception diagnosis, evidence-linked repair, mastery scoring, capability unlocks, and unaided exam mode.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the enforcement mechanism: the page structurally withholds answer keys, dynamically registers capabilities after mastery, and revokes coaching tools for exams. A general UI-driving agent cannot comparably guarantee these boundaries.
leverage_evidence: Transcript says answer key is absent from every registered tool and exam mode revokes coaching tools.
Description names live Tool Roster, four-dimensional gate, dynamic advance_exam tools, and only status/submit tools in exam mode.
execution_rationale: The transcript demonstrates a coherent progression from coaching through diagnosis, mastery, capability unlock, and tool revocation; remaining uncertainty is independent visual verification.
execution_evidence: Transcript covers cheat resistance, misconception diagnosis, evidence requirement, unlock, and unaided test.
Description specifies 17 misconceptions, four dimensions, gate threshold, and open-source/live deployment.
impact_rationale: Learners preparing for technical exams have a clear problem with answer-giving tutors; constrained retrieval practice and diagnostic feedback directly address learning quality.
impact_evidence: Specific PL-400 learner audience and exam-mode goal are stated.
Every distractor maps to a misconception and misses route to repair text.
creativity_rationale: It turns WebMCP capability registration and revocation into the pedagogy and assessment boundary itself, a deeply pursued and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Capability is treated as the guardrail rather than a prompt.
Train-aided/test-unaided transition is enacted through live tool roster changes.
usability_note: The staged learning flow is legible in the transcript; visual details not independently checked.
red_flags: The educational engine reportedly predates the agent integration; origin should distinguish new WebMCP work from pre-existing pedagogy.
Independent image inspection was blocked by vision rate limits.
standouts: WebMCP is the product's enforcement architecture.
Strong alignment between learning science, state, and tool lifecycle.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage, impact, and creativity with unusually specific evidence of the core workflow.

one_line: Agent-and-human architecture workspace connecting C4 design, infrastructure estimates, cloud comparison, ADR, and export.
what_it_does: Builds an editable C4 model, derives infrastructure needs, compares Azure/AWS estimates, records a decision, and exports a portable .workspec ZIP.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools can trace changes across canvas, infrastructure list, estimates, and ADR, avoiding fragile pointer manipulation and preserving a portable shared workspace.
leverage_evidence: Description says the agent proposes/arranges the same C4 model as the user.
Connected journey derives infrastructure, compares providers, records approval, and exports schema-validated YAML.
Claims WebMCP avoids fragile infinite-canvas automation.
execution_rationale: The product journey is coherent and unusually complete on paper, with portable artifact and import/export paths, but no visual inspection was possible.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are listed.
Description enumerates context/logical/deployment views, import/example/blank starts, validation, and CLI/enterprise compatibility.
impact_rationale: Software teams have a real problem with architecture rationale and estimates fragmenting across tools; a durable connected workspace directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Specific fragmentation problem is articulated.
Portable ZIP, Git-committable schema, and ADR capture provide credible durable value.
creativity_rationale: Connecting agent-assisted C4 design to deterministic infrastructure derivation, multi-cloud comparison, and decision records is a fresh, ambitious workflow rather than a chat wrapper.
creativity_evidence: One workspace links diagram, shopping list, cost comparison, and ADR.
Agent/human complementary responsibilities are explicitly designed into the flow.
usability_note: Connected journey and import/export improve usability, while infinite-canvas complexity remains a risk.
red_flags: No gallery images and no transcript; central workflow remains claimed rather than independently observed.
advance_reason: High-value architecture workflow and substantial WebMCP delta; advance for observed execution.
